beats.say: Why is it so hard to beat Asian Paints? Our reading: its moat is not the paint. It is the shop counter that sells it. A moat is what keeps rivals out, like water round a castle.

beats.say: And rivals have tried hard. Birla Opus was launched in twenty twenty four. Its owner, Grasim, says it had spent nearly ten thousand crore rupees building it, by March twenty twenty six. Yet by its own count, it is third by sales. So why hasn't that much money won?
beats.cap: And rivals have tried hard. Birla Opus was launched in 2024. Its owner, Grasim, says it had spent nearly ₹10,000 crore building it. That is ₹9,902 crore, by March 2026. Yet by its own count, it is third by sales. So why hasn't that much money won?

beats.say: Then came a test. From April to June twenty twenty six, most paint companies raised prices by ten percent or more, Grasim said. So dealers had a reason to buy extra, before prices went up. Dealers call that stocking up.

beats.say: In April to June, Birla Opus sold seventeen percent more than in January to March, Grasim said. Older companies grew about the same, someone noted on Grasim's call. Why? Himanshu Kapania, who heads Birla Opus, answered. As a new company, he said, we don't have the power to be able to get extra stocking. Older companies, he said, can.

beats.say: Our reading: the reason is trust. Dealers know the older names well, so they buy extra from them. Money got Birla Opus to fifty five thousand dealers, fast. Trust takes longer. That is the gap between reaching a counter and owning one.

beats.say: So is Asian Paints' moat safe? Our July twenty twenty six article tests a moat two ways. Can a rival copy it? Asian Paints passes, comfortably. Can a rival go round it? Asian Paints fails. Our reading: Birla Opus did not copy decades of dealer trust. It went round it, with money and speed.

beats.say: How is Asian Paints fighting back? With three big moves. Our July twenty twenty six article finds none of them is a price cut. One is for buyers who pay less. One is a service. One is hidden behind a factory wall.

beats.say: Move one: paint for the market that sells by weight. In January twenty twenty six, the chief executive said Asian Paints had launched Neo Bharat for it. The aim is to win buyers who now buy from small makers with no big name. At that time, it was only in some states.

beats.say: Move two runs through Raju himself: a painting service for homes. Its yearly report, out in June twenty twenty six, says dealers lead it. More than one lakh seventy five thousand customers used it. More than three thousand nine hundred dealers took part. Our reading: Raju now sells a painted home, not only a tin.

beats.say: Move three is behind a factory wall. Asian Paints is building a factory at Dahej, in Gujarat, to make a key paint chemical itself. By November twenty twenty five, it planned to spend about three thousand two hundred and fifty crore rupees. Only four or five companies in the world do this, it said in July twenty twenty six. Is it running yet?
